# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 2
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 2

---

1. And we the apostles said to him: "Lord, tell us those things which are to come: what we shall see? How shall we understand concerning the resurrection of the dead? For great and wonderful things do you tell us."

2. And the Lord showed to us a great garden, full of fair trees and blessed fruits, and of the fragrance of perfumes. Its fragrance was pleasant, and to us also there came the fragrance thereof.

3. And he showed me also the ancient man, shining in whiteness and he said to me: "This is how it shall be at the hour of their need."

4. And I, Peter, answered him: "What is this that you say? And who is the ancient man, and the children? And what is the place?"

5. And he said to me: "This garden and the trees which you see, they are the righteous dead; and the fair things you see here are those who have died for righteousness' sake."

6. "And the ancient man whom you saw — he is Moses and the law which God gave him in Mount Sinai."

7. "And the children are the little ones who have died before they committed sin, who were not full-grown. Now if this is so, then they are in the care of God."

8. And he said: "I will show you another mystery. In that day when God judges the world, the righteous shall stand before him, and the sinners shall be on the left."

9. "But some of the righteous shall shine and some shall not shine, for some have sinned and some have not sinned."

10. And I spoke to him and said: "I do not understand, but do you make it known to me."

11. And he said: "Those who shine are those who have not sinned, who have done the will of God. And those who do not shine are those who have sinned but who repented at the last."

12. "Some of the righteous were poor in this world for God's sake; and some were fasting to God, and some prayed without ceasing, and some gave freely of their substance."

13. "And all these things shall be made known at the resurrection, according to the will of God."

14. "And they shall receive the kingdom and the honor and the glory which God has prepared for them, those who have feared him."

---
*EMET note: This chapter draws heavily on the Ethiopic; the Akhmim fragment is fragmentary here. Verse structure follows Buchholz's critical edition.*
